title: Paying Center Bills from Resident Trust Fund Accounts: Standing and Per-Bill Authority
content:
**Clause.** Money moves from a Resident Trust Fund Accounts account to a center charge only with the resident's written authority: a standing authorization covers the monthly bill it names (Medicaid patient pay or private room and board) every month, while a bed-hold, ancillary or Medicare coinsurance charge needs a per-bill authorization naming that charge. A bill transfer is made only under a standing authorization covering its bill category or a per-bill authorization naming the charge. For a representative payee account, benefits are applied to the tier's monthly bill without a monthly request, and for a Medicaid payee account the personal needs allowance stays in the account. A transfer pays at most the open balance of the named charge and never exceeds the available balance. Nothing Medicare or Medicaid pays for is ever paid from the account, and an optional item or service is paid only when the resident or representative asked for it.

## Authority read from the records

The authority is the account's own record: the standing authorization recorded on the account, or a per-bill authorization in the account's list of signed requests that names the specific charge. A transfer records the charge it pays and the authorization relied on; a payee application of benefits relies on no authorization.

## Amount of a transfer

A transfer is the least of three figures: the amount authorized or requested; the open balance of the named charge on its own billing record (the charge less the payments and credits naming it); and the available balance on the transfer date (the account balance less deposits whose available date is after that date).

### Hypothetical illustration

| Amount authorized | Open balance of the charge | Available balance | Transfer |
|---|---|---|---|
| $186.40 | $142.75 | $903.11 | $142.75 |
| $186.40 | $210.00 | $903.11 | $186.40 |
| $186.40 | $210.00 | $95.20 | $95.20 |

## Points of judgement

- A standing authorization for Medicaid patient pay does not reach a bed-hold charge.
- A per-bill authorization naming one ancillary charge does not reach another ancillary charge.
